concept.name: Blue-Green & Canary Deployment Automation Pipelines
concept.tagline: Safely roll out production releases using progressive traffic routing, automated health checks, and instant rollback triggers.

spark.summary: Canary deployment incrementally shifts live user traffic (e.g. 1% -> 10% -> 100%) to a new application release version while automated metrics monitor HTTP error rates and latency for automatic rollback.
spark.keyTakeaway: Combine Canary progressive traffic routing with automated metric analysis (Prometheus/Datadog) to prevent bad releases from causing site-wide outages.

concept.whyItMatters: Deploying 100% of new code instantly risks exposing all customers to fatal bugs, database schema corruption, or performance crashes.
keyPoints: Blue-Green Deployment runs two identical environments; switches 100% traffic via router DNS/load balancer swap.
Canary Deployment routes a small fraction (e.g. 2%) of production requests to the canary pod cluster.
Automated Rollback: If canary HTTP 5xx error rate breaches 0.5%, traffic shifts back to baseline instantly.

examples.title: Netflix Kayenta Automated Canary Analysis
examples.outcome: Automatically aborts 1.2% of releases before customer impact.

tradeOffs.pro: Canary consumes far less infrastructure hardware than 2x Blue-Green clusters.
tradeOffs.con: Canary requires active database backward/forward schema compatibility.

failureModes.name: Non-Backward Compatible Schema Change
failureModes.description: Canary release drops a database column while baseline release still requires it.

commonMistakes: Relying on manual human observation to approve canary deployments.

deepDive.markdownContent: ## 📖 Argo Rollouts & Canary Traffic Shifting Architecture

caseStudy.problem: Deploying code changes 50 times per day without downtime.
caseStudy.solution: Implemented Kubernetes Argo Rollouts with automated metric analysis.
caseStudy.impact: 99.999% deployment availability across all production pipelines.

relationships.description: Canary deployments use Layer 7 load balancers to split HTTP traffic percentages.

questions.title: Canary vs Blue-Green Release Strategies
questions.prompt: What is the key advantage of Canary Deployments over Blue-Green Deployments for large-scale microservice clusters?

options.text: Canary deployments eliminate the need for automated tests.
options.explanation: Automated tests and metrics are required for canary deployments.

options.text: Canary deployments progressively shift small percentages of traffic, limiting exposure and requiring significantly less hardware duplicate capacity than full Blue-Green environment duplication.
options.explanation: Correct! Canary releases minimize blast radius and hardware overhead.

rubric.excellent: Explains blast radius restriction and hardware overhead reduction compared to Blue-Green duplication.
rubric.gap: Confuses deployment patterns with database backups.

questions.sampleSolution: Canary deployments test releases on a small traffic percentage, limiting blast radius without doubling infrastructure capacity.
questions.explanation: Progressive 1% -> 5% -> 100% traffic shifting isolates bugs to a tiny subset of production traffic.

interviewProblems.title: Zero-Downtime Continuous Deployment Pipeline
interviewProblems.scenarioPrompt: You are building the deployment engine for a global streaming service executing 100 production deployments daily across 5,000 Kubernetes pods. How do you design an automated Canary analysis and rollback pipeline?
constraints: Automatic rollback trigger latency under 10 seconds.

dimensions.name: Argo Rollouts & Traffic Weighting
dimensions.description: Using Service Mesh / NGINX ingress traffic weighting (2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%).

dimensions.name: Automated Metric Analysis & Rollback
dimensions.description: Comparing Prometheus error rates and p99 latency between canary and baseline.

interviewProblems.sampleDefense: Use Argo Rollouts on Kubernetes with Istio service mesh traffic splitting. Shift 2% traffic to canary. Compare Prometheus HTTP 5xx rates against baseline pods every 60 seconds; trigger automatic rollback if errors breach 0.5%.
commonPitfalls: Deploying breaking database schema changes before code expansion phases.
